Apple’s effective tax rate rose to 24.1 percent in fiscal 2024 from 14.7 percent in fiscal 2023 primarily because of a one‑time income‑tax charge of about $10.2 billion net tied to the State Aid Decision. In addition, the company faced a higher effective tax rate on foreign earnings and received lower tax benefits from share‑based compensation, which together pushed the overall rate higher.  

The one‑time charge alone more than doubled the provision for income taxes (from $16,741 million in 2023 to $29,749 million in 2024), illustrating how a single, non‑recurring tax event can dramatically affect the effective tax rate even when the statutory federal rate remained unchanged at 21 percent.
